angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 885,643 km at 13.89 pc = 0.85 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 72.0070 +/- 0.0974 mas (same row, RUWE 0.85): 13.89 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.273 (1.247 to 1.299) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source): 885,643 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.986 (0.946 to 1.026) from Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26; astrophysical_parameters of the same source); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5764 +/- 2 K from Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 777254360337133312: teff_gspphot 5763.587 K (16th-84th percentiles 5761.2017-5765.1753), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Andrae et al. (2023), A&A 674, A27 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 777254360337133312: teff_gspphot 5763.587 K (16th-84th percentiles 5761.2017-5765.1753), the temperature FLAME used (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202243462)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/chalawan.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.222, rounded to two decimals
